subject: Post-demo: Eval readiness & request for customer prompts / edge cases
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Eval readiness & request for customer prompts / edge cases

Hi Claire / Theo — great to meet today, thanks for walking us through the core search workflows. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned: 

Key takeaways from today
- Primary objective: Improve answer relevancy for product search and surfaced snippets (on-site and API).
- Constraints: 95th%-tile latency target 150ms, expected throughput ~120 reqs/s for pilot; must support redaction of PII (emails, phone numbers) before sending prompts to hosted evals.
- Success signal: top-3 answer precision lift on benchmark prompt set + no manual post-filtering required.

Requested from Storalyze (what we need to run an initial model-fit eval)
1) Representative prompt set (150–300 prompts) covering: exact-match queries, long-tail phrasing, multilingual (EN/ES), and adversarial/ambiguous queries. See attached sample.
2) 12–20 edge-case examples where current system fails (include expected/acceptable outputs).
3) Redaction guidance: what fields must be removed/hashed vs allowed in cleartext (PII policy).

Deliverables we’ll provide
- Recommended short-list of model candidates + expected latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Benchmark run (redwood eval harness) with comparative metrics and a short quality summary.
- Prompt-level failure analysis and suggestions for prompt engineering/filters.

Attachments: redwood_eval_info.pdf (brief on evals + what to expect). I’ve also attached a prompt template you can drop examples into; you can upload to the Drive link below or reply-all with files.

Next steps
- Can you send the prompt set and 12–20 edge cases by EOD Monday (Jan 19)? If you need a smaller starter set we can run with 50 prompts but results will be noisier.
- We’ll scope a 2-week pilot benchmark once we have the artifacts; I’ll loop in Dev for model recommendations and Marcus for product acceptance criteria.

Upload link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-storalyze-prompt-upload
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/Storalyze

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up if needed.

—Olga

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo: Eval readiness & request for customer prompts / edge cases

Hi team — quick recommendation set for Storalyze based on latency and economics: 

Short-list (reasoning + expected perf)
- Mistral-Infer-7B-Q8 (recommended starter): good latency on single-GPU, low cost; expect 60–90ms median, 120–160ms 95th depending on sequence length and batching. Good for high-throughput pilots.
- Llama-2-13B-4bit (quantized): better quality on complex paraphrase queries; 95th could be ~160–220ms unless we tune batching/KV cache. Use for quality-sensitive runs.
- Falcon-40B-infer (quantized): top quality but higher cost — use as a head-to-head comparator for precision-sensitive benchmarks.

Runtime & config recommendations (Redwood Optimize suggestions)
- Quantization profile: Q8 for the 7B; 4-bit (nf4) with per-channel for 13B/40B.
- Batch sizing: dynamic batching of 8–16 depending on concurrency; enforce latency SLO with progressive routing (pilot: route critical traffic to 7B, fallbacks to 13B for failures).
- KV cache warmup: ensure prefix caching for repeat sessions (helps if they have multi-turn search clarifications).

Prompt & eval guidance
- Accept synthetic + real mix — specify which prompts are synthetic in the CSV (column: synthetic=true/false). We’ll stratify sampling.
- Edge cases: include expected output and a short note on why current signals fail. We need 12–20 high-value failures.
- Redaction: replace PII with deterministic placeholders (e.g., <EMAIL_1>, <PHONE_1>) but keep entity types intact. Provide mapping file separately if they want reversible tokenization. For on-prem customers we recommend irreversible hashing.

Redaction quick script suggestions (we’ll include as snippet in shared doc)
- Email regex: /[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/ -> <EMAIL_n>
- Phone regex (US-focused): / (\+1)?\s?\(?\d{3}\)?[\s.-]?\d{3}[\s.-]?\d{4} / -> <PHONE_n>
- Names: use heuristics from NER (spaCy) and replace rare PHI names with <NAME_n> if required.

Artifacts we will attach for Storalyze: prompt_collection_template.csv (with columns: id, prompt, synthetic, language, expected_output, edge_case_flag) and a short runbook PDF. I’ve put a draft in the Drive folder listed below.

Benchmarks / references
- Preliminary perf baseline: https://redwood-inference.com/evals/storalyze-benchmark-2026
- Eval harness docs: https://redwood-inference.com/docs/evals/harness

If Marcus or Olga want, I can run a quick 50-prompt smoke test on Mistral-Infer-7B to show latency vs. quality tradeoff; would take ~2–3 hours to configure.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Comparator: Llama-2-13B-4bit (higher quality for paraphrase-heavy queries)
- Optional: Falcon-40B-infer for a quality head-to-head if you want a high-cost comparator

2) What we need from you by EOD Monday (Jan 26)
- Prompt set: upload CSV using the attached template or to the Drive link. Mark synthetic rows. (~150–250 prompts ideal).
- Edge cases: 12–20 examples with expected output + short note on failure mode.
- Redaction policy: confirm which entity classes must be replaced vs can remain in cleartext (we recommend emails/phones hashed or replaced).

3) What we’ll deliver after we receive the artifacts
- 2-week pilot benchmark report: latency and per-prompt precision metrics, qualitative failure list, and recommended routing/quantization profile.
- Prompt-level annotations for quick wins (filter rules, prompt edits).

If you can’t hit Jan 26 we can start with a 50-prompt smoke test (we’ll do that by Jan 22) and deliver preliminary findings.
